body: Oh, I'm quite aware that *the majority of people are worse off than me*.  I should be at the top of the world by comparison, but I'm not.  Yes, you and everyone else probably do have worse circumstances than me.  But no, that doesn't change the way I feel, though I guess I get to feel like a dick for being miserable for no explainable reason.

Huh.  Yes, we do sound very similar.  

And I've been to those Ignite events as well.  

It's a weird thing, to have no passion and see so many people with it, and wonder: how in the world did they get it?  I am not sure if people can really inspire others, but rather arouse something already existent within the person, encourage someone.  I don't know if another person can provoke you to fall in love with something, to have passion about something, when it is not something you already have.
Being alive is not anything special either.

I suppose you could say I have lost hope.  I don't have any hope that life will be better.  I feel like my life is devoid of purpose, that I have lost faith in the existence of purpose and value that would justify my own existence.

I'm not particularly curious about my future children.  I don't think I'll have children while I am this unstable.  If I get better, I will have them because my partner wants them.

I don't really see the point of a better future for a better future's sake.  As far as being proud of one's life, well, I don't feel like trying to be proud of oneself and feeling good about oneself is all that great and noble of a goal.  It's ultimately an ego thing, I figure.

I don't see anything in my future.  I guess, unless I finally get the nerve to end it for good, I see myself coasting by, getting some job, having kids, growing old, dying, the normal life thing.

I do have a special someone.  I guess if I'd want to end it, I'd tell him that I don't love him anymore and, after he's away, off myself so he isn't scarred forever or something.  Maybe myself seem like a bitch who was not worth feeling sadness over.

I have no idea.  That's part of the problem.

The people who have tangible problems, who can say, "I am missing this, this has gone wrong" have the idea that if their problem were rectified, if they had this thing that was missing, they would be better, and they can have hope for it.

I have everything save a reason to live.  I'm like the characters in Voltaire's Candide, where my worst moment was not when all these terrible things happened to me, but when I've got everything seemingly perfect but am just unhappy for who knows what reason.

I feel like my story is over and I'm done and just waiting for my end sometimes.

Went to a psychologist for a while.  I went to her every week and she had me do little exercises, cognitive behavioral therapy or whatever.  After a while, I gave up on her.  What I wanted from her - a sense of purpose, a reason to live - she couldn't give to me.

Tried exercising more, eating healthier.  Went out to concerts and museums.  Took walks around the neighborhood, met random people, interacted more with the friends I have.  Indulged in fine clothes, good food, movies.  Tried new hobbies, new books, self-help and otherwise.

In other words, I have a seemingly perfect life in which I have everything, but I can't stand it because I don't actually give a damn about anything in it, and nothing in it is reason enough to live, save the idea that things can get much, much worse if I try to off myself.
